```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5)
library(BayesianQDM)
```

This vignette describes the analysis of a proof-of-concept (PoC) study with
one time-to-event endpoint, such as progression-free survival, evaluated by
the survival probability at a milestone time. `vignette("overview")`
introduces the decision criteria.

## Model

In group $k$ ($k = t, c$), the event times are exponential with hazard
$\lambda_k$, and the data are summarized by the number of events $d_k$ and
the total observed time $E_k$, the sum of the follow-up times of all
subjects until their event or censoring (`data_tte()`). With the Gamma prior
$\lambda_k \sim \textrm{Gamma}(a_k, b_k)$ (shape $a_k$ and rate $b_k$;
`prior_gamma()`), the posterior distribution is
$$\lambda_k \mid D \sim \textrm{Gamma}(a_k + d_k, \; b_k + E_k).$$
The prior acts as $a_k$ events in a total observed time of $b_k$, so a prior
with a small shape and rate, such as `prior_gamma(0.1, 1)` with time in
months, has little influence.

The effect is the difference of the survival probabilities at the milestone
time $t_0$,
$$\theta = S_t(t_0) - S_c(t_0), \qquad S_k(t_0) = \exp(-\lambda_k t_0).$$
The posterior probability $\Pr(\theta > q \mid D)$ is computed by numerical
integration over the control hazard (`psurvdiff()`).

External data with $d_e$ events and total observed time $E_e$ enter through
a power prior with weight $a_0$, which adds $a_0 d_e$ to the shape and
$a_0 E_e$ to the rate. A hypothetical control adds its events and total
observed time to the prior of the control group.

## Decision for observed data

A single-arm study is often compared with a known benchmark. With
`fixed_c`, the control survival probability at the milestone is a known
value $S_{c0}$, and the probabilities of the Go and NoGo regions are Gamma
probabilities of the treatment hazard. Consider 30 subjects, a milestone of
3 months, a benchmark of 0.72, $\theta_{TV} = 0.15$ and
$\theta_{MAV} = 0$:

```{r design}
crit <- criterion_posterior(theta_tv = 0.15, theta_mav = 0,
                            gamma_go = 0.6, gamma_nogo = 0.8)
des <- design_tte(n_t = 30, n_c = 0, prior_t = prior_gamma(0.1, 1),
                  criterion = crit, milestone = 3, fixed_c = 0.72)
dec <- qdm_decide(des, data_t = data_tte(events = 6, exposure = 150))
dec
```

The Go region is $S_t(3) > 0.72 + 0.15$, that is
$\lambda_t < -\log(0.87) / 3$, whose posterior probability is

```{r fixed-check}
pgamma(-log(0.87) / 3, shape = 0.1 + 6, rate = 1 + 150)
```

With `fixed_c = 0`, the effect is the milestone survival probability
itself, and the thresholds are survival probabilities.

With a concurrent control group of 30 subjects:

```{r concurrent}
des_c <- design_tte(n_t = 30, n_c = 30, prior_t = prior_gamma(0.1, 1),
                    prior_c = prior_gamma(0.1, 1), criterion = crit,
                    milestone = 3)
dec_c <- qdm_decide(des_c, data_t = data_tte(6, 150),
                    data_c = data_tte(12, 140))
dec_c
post_t <- dec_c$posterior_t
post_c <- dec_c$posterior_c
psurvdiff(0.15, milestone = 3, shape_t = post_t[["shape"]],
          rate_t = post_t[["rate"]], shape_c = post_c[["shape"]],
          rate_c = post_c[["rate"]], lower.tail = FALSE)
```

External control data and hypothetical controls are given as in the other
vignettes, with `borrow(data_tte(...), a0)` and
`hypothetical(data_tte(...))`.

## Conduct of the study

The operating characteristics and the predictive criterion need the timing
of the study, which `conduct_tte()` specifies: the enrollment
(piecewise uniform over the intervals of `accrual_time` with relative rates
`accrual_rate`), the dropout (piecewise exponential hazards) and the time of
the analysis, either at a calendar time (`cut_time`) or at the time of a
given number of events among all subjects of the study (`cut_events`). For
example, enrollment over 15 months with increasing rates, a small dropout
hazard and an analysis 15.44 months after the start of enrollment:

```{r conduct}
cond <- conduct_tte(accrual_time = c(0, 5, 10, 15),
                    accrual_rate = c(0.4, 2, 4.5),
                    dropout_hazard = 0.00226, cut_time = 15.44)
cond
des <- design_tte(n_t = 30, n_c = 0, prior_t = prior_gamma(0.1, 1),
                  criterion = crit, milestone = 3, conduct = cond,
                  fixed_c = 0.72)
```

## Predictive criterion

For the predictive criterion, a future study with $m_t$ and $m_c$ subjects
is conducted as specified by `conduct_future` (by default `conduct`). The
survival probability of each group in the future study is estimated by
$\exp\{-t_0 (a + \tilde d) / (b + \tilde E)\}$, from its number of events
$\tilde d$ and total observed time $\tilde E$, and the future effect is the
difference of the two estimates (or the treatment estimate minus the fixed
value). The predictive probabilities are estimated by simulating `nMC`
future studies, each with hazards drawn from the posterior distributions,
so they are Monte Carlo estimates and depend on the seed:

```{r predictive}
des_pred <- design_tte(
  n_t = 30, n_c = 0, prior_t = prior_gamma(0.1, 1),
  criterion = criterion_predictive(theta_null = 0.05, m_t = 60,
                                   gamma_go = 0.8, gamma_nogo = 0.3),
  milestone = 3, conduct = cond, fixed_c = 0.72, nMC = 5000
)
qdm_decide(des_pred, data_t = data_tte(6, 150), seed = 1)
```

## Operating characteristics

A scenario gives the median survival time of each group (`median_t` and,
with a concurrent control group, `median_c`), and the hazard is
$\log 2$ divided by the median. `qdm_oc()` simulates `nsim` studies
conducted as specified by `conduct`, with the same random numbers for all
scenarios. The median for which the milestone survival equals the benchmark
is `med0` below, and the median for which it equals the benchmark plus
$\theta_{TV}$ is `med1`:

```{r oc}
med0 <- 3 * log(2) / -log(0.72)
med1 <- 3 * log(2) / -log(0.72 + 0.15)
c(med0, med1)
scen <- data.frame(median_t = c(6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20))
oc <- qdm_oc(des, scen, seed = 1)
oc
plot(oc)
```

The horizontal axis is the survival probability of the treatment group at
the milestone, and the vertical lines are shifted by the fixed control
value. For a design with a concurrent control group, the probabilities of
each simulated study are computed by numerical integration, which takes
longer; here 1000 studies are simulated per scenario:

```{r oc-concurrent}
des_c <- design_tte(n_t = 30, n_c = 30, prior_t = prior_gamma(0.1, 1),
                    prior_c = prior_gamma(0.1, 1), criterion = crit,
                    milestone = 3, conduct = cond)
oc_c <- qdm_oc(des_c, data.frame(median_t = c(med0, 10, 15, 20),
                                 median_c = med0), nsim = 1000, seed = 1)
oc_c
```

With a predictive criterion, every simulated study requires `nMC` simulated
future studies, so small values of `nsim` and `nMC` are advisable for
exploration.

## Calibration of the thresholds

The thresholds of the single-arm design are calibrated so that the Go
criterion is met with probability at most 0.05 when the milestone survival
equals the benchmark (median `med0`), and the NoGo criterion with
probability at most 0.1 when it equals the benchmark plus 0.15 (median
`med1`):

```{r calibrate}
cal <- qdm_calibrate(des, scenario_go = data.frame(median_t = med0),
                     scenario_nogo = data.frame(median_t = med1),
                     target_go = 0.05, target_nogo = 0.1, seed = 1)
cal
plot(cal)
```

The chosen thresholds are $\gamma_{go} =$ `r cal$gamma_go` and
$\gamma_{nogo} =$ `r cal$gamma_nogo`.

## Decision boundary

`qdm_boundary()` gives the decision for each combination of the number of
events and the total observed time of the treatment group. With a posterior
criterion, it does not depend on the conduct of the study:

```{r boundary}
b <- qdm_boundary(des, exposure_t = seq(20, 400, by = 5))
plot(b)
```

With a total observed time of 150 months, a Go decision needs at most
`r max(b$events_t[b$exposure_t == 150 & b$decision == "Go"])` events. For a
design with a concurrent control group, the observed control data are given
by `data_c`.
